text:
I am continuing to monitor the recovery efforts in Copperhill and am working with our federal and state partners to ensure that the people of this area receive all available assistance during this cleanup and restoration.

FEMA has been on site since November 9th, and I have personally been in close contact with the Regional Director, TEMA officials, and the county and city mayors about conditions on the ground and the needs of those affected. My team and I will continue to do all we can at the federal level to help secure the resources our communities need.

Tennessee Fire Mutual Aid swift-water teams conducted more than 100 rescues across Tennessee and Georgia. I am grateful for their service and for our first responders, emergency personnel, volunteers, and everyone helping their neighbors during this difficult time.

The evacuation order for Copperhill has been lifted, and cleanup and debris removal efforts continue in affected areas. Residents should follow updates from local officials and enter damaged or debris-filled areas only when it is safe. Before beginning cleanup, take photographs and document damage and debris for insurance and recovery purposes.

This recovery will take days, weeks, and months, and I will continue to do all I can to ensure federal resources reach this community in need and encourage others to seek opportunities to provide needed donations to help its residents.
